about: Links this machine to its Nerve centers.

global.about: Where node.toml and the keys live [env: NERVE_CONFIG_DIR] [default: ~/.config/nerve, or /etc/nerve when installed as a service]

sections.about: Run the node as a service under a user of its own (Linux with sudo, Windows as administrator), set it up, keep it current, and back it up or move it.

verbs.about: Install the node as a service that starts with the machine and runs under a user of its own, make the account nerve-run for its commands and take you as the owner (Linux with sudo from your own account, Windows as administrator)

args.about: Run by root itself (Linux): `root` makes root the owner, so that user mode, and allowlist mode as the owner, run commands as root, with every right on the machine and over Nerve; needs --accept-root-owner. At a terminal install asks instead, and an owner root confirmed before stays. `none` leaves the node without an owner, root or another
args.name: --owner <ACCOUNT>

args.about: Confirms --owner=root: you accept that nothing in Nerve holds those commands back
args.name: --accept-root-owner

verbs.name: install

verbs.about: Stop and remove the service, nerve-run and its entries on your folders, the node's user and the program; the config and state folders stay

args.about: Delete the config and state folders too: the keys, the pairings and the audit log
args.name: --purge

verbs.name: uninstall

verbs.about: Name the node, choose where it keeps its keys, pair the first center and choose its mode and folder, one question at a time
verbs.name: setup

verbs.about: Replace the installed program with the latest release and restart the service; config, keys and audit log stay

args.about: Take the new program from this file instead of downloading the latest release
args.name: --from <FILE>

verbs.name: update

shared_args.about: Read the passphrase from the first line of this file instead of asking; `-` reads it from stdin
shared_args.name: --passphrase-file <FILE>

verbs.about: Write the config and the keys to a file that a passphrase protects, to keep or to move the node to another machine

args.about: The file to write. It is private to you (mode 0600)
args.name: <FILE>

args.about: Also take the keys that are in the system keyring into the file; without it they stay there and are left out
args.name: --include-keyring

args.about: Replace the file when it exists
args.name: --overwrite

verbs.name: backup

verbs.about: Put the config and keys of a backup in place of this node's. The node must not run

args.about: The backup file
args.name: <FILE>

args.about: Replace a node here that is not the one the backup is of
args.name: --replace

args.about: Keep the keys in `file` or in the system `keyring` here, whatever the backup's config says
args.name: --secret-storage <file|keyring>

args.about: Leave the proxy out of the restored config, with its password and header values; set it again on this machine
args.name: --without-proxy

verbs.name: restore

sections.about: Every center has its own rights on this machine.

verbs.about: Show each center's mode, or choose how much a center may do: only what allow rules name, what each folder allows (as nerve-run, an account of its own), or all you can do (as you)

args.about: `allowlist` (only what an allow rule names, as nerve-run), `folder` (what each folder's rights allow, as nerve-run, the default; on the installed node a file call may also read what every account may read) or `user` (anything you could do yourself, as you, protected files aside). Without it, each center's mode is shown
args.name: <MODE>

args.about: End the mode after this many hours: user goes back to the mode before it, folder to allowlist (without it they stay until you change them)
args.name: --for <HOURS>

args.about: With allowlist: run the allowed commands as you instead of as nerve-run, outside the folders' sandbox (installed node, Linux)
args.name: --as-owner

verbs.name: mode

cards.about: Show a center's folders, or choose the folders it may use and what it may do in each

verbs.about: Show a center's folders, or choose the folders it may use and what it may do in each
verbs.name: folder

verbs.about: Let a center use a folder, or change what it may do in one it has: `r` reads, `w` writes, `x` runs commands (`rw`, `rx`); `none` closes a folder inside one it may use

args.about: The rights, one word: `r`, `rw`, `rwx` and so on, or `none`
args.name: <RIGHTS>

verbs.name: folder add

verbs.about: Take a folder away from a center

verbs.about: Give nerve-run its access to everything in the folders of every center again, also what was moved into them (the installed node on Linux): a pass over every granted folder
verbs.name: folder sync

verbs.about: Keep a center's commands off the network, or let them on it again: `off` lets them open no socket but a unix one, in every mode, and no sudo-list command runs; where they run as you (user mode, allowlist --as-owner) or the machine cannot hold them, none of them runs

args.about: `off` or `on`
args.name: <STATE>

verbs.name: network

cards.about: Show a center's rules, or keep its lists of commands that are allowed, forbidden or run with sudo

verbs.about: Show a center's rules, or keep its lists of commands that are allowed, forbidden or run with sudo

args.about: The list to show: `allow`, `deny` or `sudo`; all three if left out
args.name: <LIST>

verbs.name: rule

verbs.about: Put a command on a list; one that starts with `sudo` goes on the sudo list. A trailing ` *` covers every command that starts so (`'git status *'`)

args.about: The list: `allow` (may run in allowlist mode; a sudo command may run with sudo while sudo is on) or `deny` (a command line that matches never runs, in any mode)
args.name: <LIST>

args.about: The command line; a trailing ` *` covers every command that starts with the words before it
args.name: <COMMAND>

args.about: Make the rule of an audit entry of this action instead, as the audit buttons do: `fs.read` takes a path (`/srv/data/*` covers the folder), an action without a target takes "" (`*` covers its capability)
args.name: --action <CAP.ACTION>

args.about: With --action: hold the rule to one argument of the call, as the audit buttons do: `--arg room=office` makes `lamp.set:room=office`
args.name: --arg <FIELD=VALUE>

verbs.name: rule add

verbs.about: Take an entry off its list: the entry as `rule` shows it, or the command line that made it

args.about: The list (`allow`, `deny` or `sudo`), needed only when the entry is on two; then the entry
args.name: <ENTRY>

verbs.name: rule rm

verbs.about: Change one entry of a list in place, as one change: the entry as `rule` shows it, and what it becomes

args.about: The list: `allow`, `deny` or `sudo`
args.name: <LIST>

args.about: The entry as `rule` shows it
args.name: <ENTRY>

args.about: What it becomes: an entry as `rule` shows them (`exec.run:git status`, `fs.read:~/notes/*`; on the sudo list a sudo command's pattern), or a plain command line, which becomes the rule `add` makes of it
args.name: <NEW>

cards.about: Show every capability, turn capabilities and single actions on or off, and declare capabilities of your own in node.toml
cards.name: cap

shared_args.about: What it does: read, write, execute, sense or actuate. Sense and actuate need your `cap set NAME on` for a center
shared_args.name: --effect <EFFECT>

shared_args.about: One line for the agent: what it does
shared_args.name: --summary <SUMMARY>

shared_args.about: The JSON Schema of its arguments, an object; `none` takes no arguments; `-` reads it from stdin. A property marked "x-nerve-path": "read" or "write" is a path the node holds to the folders
shared_args.name: --params <JSON>

shared_args.about: What it returns: `text`, what the command prints (the default), or a JSON Schema the printed JSON must fit; `-` reads it from stdin
shared_args.name: --result <text|JSON>

shared_args.about: How long it may run, in seconds, up to limits.max_timeout_secs; `default` for the node's default
shared_args.name: --timeout <SECS>

shared_args.about: Where it runs: any (the default), linux or windows. A node offers only those of its platform
shared_args.name: --platform <PLATFORM>

verbs.about: Show every capability, turn capabilities and single actions on or off, and declare capabilities of your own in node.toml

args.about: Only this center's settings
args.name: --center <CENTER>

verbs.name: cap

verbs.about: Set a capability (`fs`) or one action (`exec.run`) to on, off or hidden

args.about: The capability (`fs`) or action (`exec.run`)
args.name: <CAP>

args.about: `on`, `off` or `hidden`
args.name: <SETTING>

verbs.name: cap set

verbs.about: Declare a capability of your own, NAME (`cap.action`, like sensors.read), that runs a fixed command: the words after `--`, the program first. A word written `{field}` is the call's argument `field`, as one whole argument; no shell reads it. It runs as nerve-run on the installed Linux node, held to the folders; a node run by hand offers none

args.about: `cap.action`, like sensors.read
args.name: <NAME>

args.about: The program and its arguments, after `--`
args.name: <COMMAND>

verbs.name: cap add

verbs.about: Change a capability you declared: what you give replaces what it has, and a command after `--` its command

args.about: The program and its arguments, after `--`
args.name: <COMMAND>

verbs.name: cap edit

verbs.about: Remove a capability you declared; it leaves every center at once. With --center, remove one that center added itself (settings on); `cap set NAME off --center` turns it off instead

args.about: The center that added it, for a capability a center added
args.name: --center <CENTER>

verbs.name: cap rm

cards.about: Show the programs that may add capabilities (providers), allow one, or remove it
cards.name: provider

verbs.about: Show the programs that may add capabilities (providers), allow one, or remove it
verbs.name: provider

verbs.about: Let the program EXE attach as the provider NAME; it replaces the program allowed under that name. The node checks that the program that attaches runs this very file

args.about: The provider's name, which its capabilities carry: 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and `-`
args.name: <NAME>

args.about: The full path of the program's executable
args.name: <EXE>

verbs.name: provider add

verbs.about: Remove the program allowed as NAME; its capabilities leave at once

args.about: The provider's name
args.name: <NAME>

verbs.name: provider rm

cards.about: Show or choose the proxy the node uses to reach centers
cards.name: proxy

verbs.about: Show or choose the proxy the node uses to reach centers
verbs.name: proxy

verbs.about: Reach centers through an HTTP proxy. Header values and a password are kept in the system keyring, never in node.toml; the installed node on Windows takes neither

args.about: The proxy, http://host:port, or http://user:password@host:port when it wants a login (http://user@host:port asks for the password, or reads it from the first line of stdin); https://... for another proxy reached over TLS; or the nerve://relay link a relay showed, which holds its address, pin and this node's token
args.name: <URL>

args.about: The pin of an https:// proxy's certificate (a relay's: `nerve-node relay` there shows it); without it the system's roots check it
args.name: --pin <PIN>

args.about: A header for the proxy, `Name: value`; can be given more than once. The value goes into the system keyring. `-` reads headers from stdin, one a line, after the password
args.name: --header <NAME: VALUE>

verbs.name: proxy set

verbs.about: Reach centers directly again, and delete the proxy's values from the system keyring
verbs.name: proxy off

cards.about: Let nodes that cannot reach a center themselves reach this node's centers through it
cards.name: relay

verbs.about: Let nodes that cannot reach a center themselves reach this node's centers through it
verbs.name: relay

verbs.about: Turn the relay on: listen for other nodes at ADDRESS, like 0.0.0.0:7490. A node reaches only this node's own https centers through it

args.about: The address and port to listen on, like 0.0.0.0:7490 or [::]:7490
args.name: <ADDRESS>

args.about: Tunnels at once, over every relayed node (16 unless set)
args.name: --max-links <N>

args.about: Tunnels at once of one relayed node (4 unless set)
args.name: --max-links-per-node <N>

args.about: Tunnels one relayed node may open a minute, every node alike (30 unless set; for a relay behind this one, use `relay set <name>`)
args.name: --max-opens-per-minute <N>

verbs.name: relay on

verbs.about: Turn the relay off: stop listening and end every tunnel. The nodes and their tokens stay
verbs.name: relay off

verbs.about: Let a node use the relay: makes its token and shows it once, in a link the other node pastes. Without --to its tunnels may go to every https center of this node

args.about: The relayed node's name here, 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting and ending with a letter or digit
args.name: <NAME>

args.about: A center of this node the relayed node may reach; can be given more than once. Without it, every one
args.name: --to <CENTER>

args.about: Where the other node reaches this machine, HOST or HOST:PORT, for its link (without it: the address the relay listens on, else this machine's host name)
args.name: --address <HOST[:PORT]>

verbs.name: relay add

verbs.about: Change what a relayed node may: the centers it may reach (its tunnels to others end), and limits of its own in place of the relay's, for a relay behind this one, which carries many nodes. What is not given stays

args.about: A center of this node the relayed node may reach; can be given more than once; `*` for every one
args.name: --to <CENTER>

args.about: Its tunnels at once; `default` for the relay's --max-links-per-node
args.name: --max-links <N>

args.about: The tunnels it may open a minute; `default` for the relay's
args.name: --max-opens-per-minute <N>

verbs.name: relay set

verbs.about: Give a relayed node a new token and end the tunnels of the old one; its centers and limits stay. Shows the token once, in a link the other node pastes

args.about: Where the other node reaches this machine, HOST or HOST:PORT, for its link (as for `relay add`)
args.name: --address <HOST[:PORT]>

verbs.name: relay token

verbs.about: Take a node's token away and end its tunnels
verbs.name: relay rm
